newsitem.title: Sri lanka: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Government decides to put back clock by half an hour from midnight Friday, placing Sri Lanka six hours ahead of GMT. Sri Lanka put the clock forward by one hour on May 24 to make maximum use of daylight in the wake of a severe power crisis due to drought.
World Cup winning Sri Lankan cricketers to get salary raise, the Board of Control for Cricket says. Sri Lankan cricketers last received a pay hike in 1994.

Police commandoes begin search for trouble-makers in the southern Yala national park. Recently, unknown persons created disturbances in the park by abducting park workers and hijacking vehicles. Yala is one of tropical Sri Lanka's main tourist attractions.

Bail refused to suspected Swiss paedophile who was remanded till October 30. The man, who runs several businesses in Sri Lanka and owns a house in the coastal town of Negombo, was arrested on October 17 in connection with alleged sex offences with children.
Government launches ambitious house to house programme of educating masses on its proposed devolution peace plan, to end the island's 13 year-old war with separatist Tamil rebels.
Twenty three members of parliament urge government to involve Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in its proposed peace plan aimed at ending the country's 13 year-old ethnic war.

Hundreds including Buddhist monks, stage sit-in at a popular temple near Colombo, against government plans to privatise the State Steel Corporation. The Sri Lankan government's plan to sell loss-making state owned enterprises has run into opposition mainly from left-wing political parties.
